description.value: Structural MRI voxel-based morphometry study examining overlapping orbitofrontal gray matter volume reductions related to body mass index and duration of cocaine use in healthy controls and cocaine-dependent individuals.

spans.text: overlapping reductions in orbitofrontal gray matter volume relating to body mass index were seen in healthy control and cocaine-dependent individuals, as well as in relation to duration of cocaine abuse

value: We hypothesized there would be overlapping regions of OFC volume decline corresponding to years of cocaine use and BMI in these individuals.

description.value: Human neuroimaging study comparing previously published healthy control and cocaine-dependent samples using structural MRI; groups were analyzed separately and directly compared.

spans.text: We compared structural magnetic resonance imaging scans of a previously published sample of 60 healthy control volunteers with body mass indexes (BMI)s ranging from normal weight to obese (17.8–33.5, mean = 25.5) and 60 cocaine-dependent individuals with similar BMIs (16.6–32.7, mean = 24.2) and a span of 31 years of cocaine use (mean = 9.8 years) (Ersche et al . 2011 ).

value: The cocaine-related decline in gray matter overlapped with BMI-related reductions bilaterally in the superior orbitofrontal gyrus, middle orbitofrontal gyrus and left gyrus rectus (Brodmann Area 11).
